resposta: How it works: You're taught that you're born in debt and you're never good enough. Guilt becomes permanent, and forgiveness only comes through the institution. Example: sermons that remind you every week how unworthy you are, without ever announcing peace.
aprofundar: How to recognize: You feel guilty even for thinking, for resting, for having fun, and for relief only when you do what the group tells you to do. Lifton called it a requirement of purity and cult of confession. Note that the prophet Ezekiel already said, in chapter 18: the son shall not bear the guilt of the father.
camada3: How to free yourself: separate the healthy guilt, which points to a real mistake and asks for redress, from the toxic guilt, which accuses your being. Paul wrote, in Romans eight: there is no condemnation. To contemplate: Whose voice is accusing you inside?

resposta: How it works: Threatened with hell, curse or disgrace to anyone who disobeys, doubts, leaves or doesn't hurt. Example: If you leave the church, your family will be cursed.
aprofundar: How to recognize: the threat cannot be verified, but the fear is real and immediate; and the threat is the one that offers protection. It's the problem and solution pair. Say fear of hell to see the full story of that idea.
camada3: How to break free: remember that love does not threaten. 1 John 4:18: perfect love throws out fear. To ponder: Would a God of love need a threat to be loved?

tema: The Terror of the End Times
palavras: date of the end of the world
the terror of the end times
resposta: How it works: Announce that the end is near, sometimes with a date set, to create urgency: sell everything, donate everything, obey now. Historical example: The preacher William Miller dated Christ's return to 1844; it did not happen, and the episode became known as the Great Deception. Harold Camping set it for 2011.
aprofundar: How to recognize: urgency, date, request for money or break up with family. Jesus said, at Matthew 24:36, of that day and hour no one knows. And Deuteronomy, chapter eighteen, verse twenty-two, teaches that if what the prophet says does not come to pass, he has spoken presumptuously.
camada3: How to break free: No big decision is made in a hurry. Wait, check with people on the outside, check the same leader's past prophecies. To ponder: If the world ended tomorrow, would you still choose to live in fear today?

resposta: How it works: The donation is presented as an investment with a guaranteed return: sow to reap, make a pact, give what you don't have. Example: campaigns that promise healing, employment, or marriage in exchange for a high-value offer.
aprofundar: How to recognize: there is the promise of material return, public pressure, suggested values and blame for failure. Robert Cialdini described reciprocity as one of the principles of persuasion: whoever receives something feels obligated to give back, and here it reverses, you give expecting God to be obligated. But Paul wrote, at 2 Corinthians 9, that each one should give as he has resolved in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion.
camada3: How to free yourself: Give, if you will, out of gratitude and accountability, never as a purchase. In Acts 8, Peter rebukes those who wanted to buy God's gift. To ponder: Would God need money?

resposta: How it works: You're taught that you're only protected under the umbrella of the leader, and that disobeying him is disobeying God. Example: needing permission from the pastor to get married, change jobs or town.
aprofundar: How to recognize: The leader decides over his personal life, is not accountable, and treats any question as rebellion. In the BITE model, it's behavior control. Milgram showed how ordinary people obey authority even against their conscience.
camada3: How to break free: Remember Matthew 23: One is your teacher, and you are all brothers; and from Mark 10: whoever wants to be great must be your servant. Healthy leadership accepts being questioned. To contemplate: who covers the leader?

palavras: don t touch the anointed one
you can t criticize the pastor
resposta: How it works: Psalm 105 is used, verse 15, "Touch not my anointed", to prohibit any criticism of the leader. For example, one who reports an abuse is accused of touching the anointed and threatened with punishment.
aprofundar: How to recognize: Read the context. In verses nine to fifteen, the psalm speaks of the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, protected from foreign kings. In the story of David and Saul, in 1 Samuel 24, not touching is not physically hurting, and not forbidding speech. The prophet Nathan confronted King David about his sin, as recorded at 2 Samuel 12.
camada3: How to break free: The Beroeans, at Acts 17:11, examined the Scriptures to see if what Paul said was true, and they were commended for it. True criticism is not attacking. To ponder, why would a man of God fear being examined?

resposta: How it works: Doubt is called enemy attack, lack of faith, or rebellion. So one becomes a policeman of one's own mind. Example: that's the devil putting thoughts in your head.
aprofundar: How to recognize: You're afraid to think about certain questions. Lifton called sacred science, the doctrine that cannot be questioned, and loaded language, the clichés that enclose thought. In the BITE model, it's thought control.
camada3: How to break free: Paul wrote, examine all things and hold fast to what is fine, 1 Thessalonians 5:21, and John, prove the spirits, 1 John 4:1. A truth is not afraid of questions. To reflect: How would you know if you were wrong?

palavras: they re friends of the church
don t mix with the world
nao se misture com o mundo
resposta: How it works: It teaches that the world outside is the devil's, that the unbelieving family is the enemy, and that only the group is safe. Example: discouraging friendships, studies, and programs outside the church.
aprofundar: How to recognize: your whole social life is inside the group, you only get information from it and you're afraid of people outside. Lifton called it environmental control, and the BITE model information control.
camada3: How to break free: Build bridges, little by little, with family and friends outside. Jesus ate with publicans and sinners. To ponder: Would a group that has the truth need to hide you from the world?

resposta: How it works: On arrival, the person receives undue attention, praise, and affection, and finally feels loved. Then that love becomes conditional on obedience. The term love bombing was used in the 1970's in connection with the Unification Church, and today it applies to cults and abusive relationships.
aprofundar: How to recognize: too much intensity too soon, too much haste for you to commit, and a sudden coldness when you disagree or fail. Cialdini described affection: we say yes to whom we like.
camada3: How to break free: True love doesn't change when you disagree. Notice what happens the day you say no. To contemplate: Is this affection for you, or for what you can give to the group?

resposta: How it works: Anyone who errs or disagrees is exposed in front of everyone, removed from office or banned from participating. The fear of shame keeps the rest in line. Example: announcing from the pulpit the name of the one who is in discipline.
aprofundar: How to recognize: Punishment is public, disproportionate, and an example to others. Lifton called it a cult of confession: intimacy became an instrument of control.
camada3: How to be free: Remember that Jesus, before the woman who was about to be stoned, said: "Let the one who is without sin cast the first stone". True correction is discreet and restorative. To ponder: Does such discipline heal a person, or does it protect power?

palavras: i m nothing without the church
without the group, i m nothing
nao sou nada sem a igreja
sem o grupo nao sou nada
resposta: How it works: the group becomes your whole identity, your family, your agenda, your vocabulary and your value. Without it, you feel like a nobody. Example: every night of the week taken up with worship and homework.
aprofundar: How to recognize: You no longer know who is outside the group, and the thought of leaving causes panic. Lifton called it the doctrine above the person: actual experience is worth less than what the group says.
camada3: How to break free: cultivate something unique to you, a talent, a study, a friendship, a walk. Their identity predates any group. To contemplate: who were you before you came in, and who do you want to be now?

resposta: How it works: repetitive music, lights, fatigue, worship hours and collective shouting lead to a state of strong emotion, in which criticism drops. That's when the call comes, the money request or the decision. Example: the offer requested at the height of emotion.
aprofundar: How to recognize: emotion is not proof of truth. The same effects appear at concerts, rallies and cheerleaders. Cialdini shows the social proof: we do what we see others do. Emotion itself is beautiful; the problem is using it as leverage.
camada3: How to break free: Never make important decisions or give money at the height of emotion. Go home, sleep, and decide quietly. To contemplate: what remains in you the next day when the music stops?

resposta: How it works: A promise of healing, a miracle, or prosperity in exchange for an offering, an anointing, a campaign, or payment. Documented example: In 1986, researcher James Randi revealed that televangelist Peter Popoff received, by electronic means, the information he claimed to come from God.
aprofundar: How to recognize: price, urgency, unverified testimony, and guilt by lack of faith when it doesn't work. The worst risk: abandoning medical treatment. Jesus said, in Matthew 10: freely you have received, freely give.
camada3: How to get out: Never leave a treatment without talking to your doctor. Prayer and medicine are not enemies. To contemplate: If the miracle is from God, why does it have a price?

palavras: whoever gets out goes to hell
quem sai vai para o inferno
resposta: How it works: whoever leaves is called a deviant, a traitor, or a loser, and often loses family and friends all at once. The fear of that rejection keeps people for years in a place that already hurts them. Lifton called for the dispensation of existence: those who are outside have no value.
aprofundar: How to recognize: You stay not because of conviction, but because of fear of what they will say or do. Ask me, if I left, would anyone still love me?
camada3: How to break free: Leave, if necessary, with a plan, a support network, and, if possible, professional help. Staying in the faith is also a legitimate choice when you are free. In Brazil, the CVV answers at 188. To ponder: Is faith that is held only by the fear of going out still faith?

tema: The Inquisition in numbers and tortures
palavras: how many died in the inquisition
the inquisition in numbers and tortures
resposta: The figures that historical research supports: Spanish Inquisition, 1478 to 1834, about one hundred and fifty thousand tried and three to five thousand executed. Portuguese, from 1536 to 1821, about thirty to forty thousand trials, with one hundred and seventy-five burned in person, according to Henry Lea. Roman, after 1542, about one thousand two hundred and fifty death sentences, according to Andrea Del Col. Witch hunts in Europe, forty to sixty thousand executed, about eighty percent women, mostly by secular and local courts, Catholic and Protestant.
aprofundar: Torture was authorized by the bull Ad extirpanda of Pope Innocent IV in 1252. The best-known methods are the pole, or hook, which suspended the person by the wrists; the colt, a rope-bound easel; and the toca, water torture. The suffering went beyond the deaths: confiscation of property, the sambenito, clothes of shame worn in public, anonymous denunciations among neighbors and the expulsion of the Jews from Spain in 1492, from forty to a hundred thousand people. From Brazil, which never had a court of its own, prisoners were sent to Lisbon; the Rio de Janeiro playwright Antônio José da Silva, the Jew, was guillotined and burned in 1739.
camada3: Myths that don't hold up: the nine million burned witches have no basis, and the iron maiden is a 19th-century invention. The truth weighs enough already without exaggeration. On Indulgence Day, March 12, 2000, Pope John Paul II apologized for the methods of intolerance used in the service of truth. Find out more at the source links.

tema: The Crusades and the Sack of Constantinople
palavras: the crusades and the sack of constantinople
resposta: The Crusades were wars called by popes, beginning in 1095, with the promise of forgiveness of sins to the combatants. In April 1204, the Fourth Crusade, which was to go to Jerusalem, plundered Constantinople, a Christian city, with massacres, rapes, and theft of relics, defying Pope Innocent III's prohibition.
aprofundar: In 1099 at the taking of Jerusalem, chroniclers of the time described a massacre of Muslims and Jews. Historians disagree about the exact numbers, and so they are not given here as certain. Pope John Paul II in 2001 apologized to Orthodox Christians for the sack of 1204.
camada3: To contemplate: the promise of salvation was used as payment for a war. When heaven is offered as a reward for killing, what happened to the sacred?

resposta: On July 22, 1209, in the Albigensian Crusade against the Cathars of southern France, the city of Béziers was taken and the population massacred, including people taking refuge in the church. The pope's successor, Arnaud Amalric, wrote that almost twenty thousand were killed, his number probably exaggerated.
aprofundar: The phrase kill them all, God will recognize his own, is attributed to the legacy, but was not recorded until some thirty years later, by the monk Caesar of Heisterbach, and its authenticity is disputed. The crusade paved the way for the medieval Inquisition.
camada3: To contemplate: the Cathars were persecuted for believing differently. How many times in history has disagreement been treated as a crime?

resposta: The Spanish Inquisition was established in 1478 and abolished in 1834. He persecuted mainly Jewish converts accused of maintaining the old faith, then Muslim converts and Protestants. It is estimated that some 150,000 were tried and 3,000 to 5,000 executed.
aprofundar: On March 31, 1492, the Decree of the Alhambra expelled Jews who would not convert; modern estimates range from forty to a hundred thousand expelled. Pope Sixtus IV himself, in 1482, denounced the greed of the inquisitors of Aragon, who were interested in the confiscated goods.
camada3: To contemplate: persecution came along with confiscation. When the prosecution profits the accuser, the truth no longer matters.

resposta: The Portuguese Inquisition ran from 1536 to 1821. According to Henry Lea, between 1540 and 1794 there were one thousand one hundred and seventy-five burned in person, six hundred and thirty-three in effigy, and more than twenty-nine thousand penitents. The file has more than thirty-five thousand cases.
aprofundar: Brazil never had its own court, but received visits, the first between 1591 and 1595, in Bahia and Pernambuco, and the prisoners were sent to Lisbon. The most persecuted were the new Christians, Jews forcibly converted in 1497. The playwright Antônio José da Silva, born in Rio de Janeiro, was guillotined and burned in Lisbon on October 19, 1739.
camada3: To reflect: Many Brazilians are descended from new Christians who hid their origins out of fear. What other parts of our history have been hidden by fear?

resposta: The philosopher and friar Giordano Bruno was burned alive by the Roman Inquisition on February 17, 1600, in Campo de' Fiori, Rome, after a seven-year trial. He advocated, among other ideas, an infinite universe with countless worlds.
aprofundar: Fact: He was condemned mainly for theological theses, such as denying the Trinity and the divinity of Christ, and not just for astronomy. Even so, he was killed for his ideas. Today there is a statue of him in the same place.
camada3: To reflect: Bruno reportedly told the judges that they might be more afraid to pass sentence than he was of receiving it. Who has the truth needs to burn who thinks differently?

resposta: On June 22, 1633, the Roman Inquisition condemned Galileo on the strong suspicion of heresy for advocating that the earth revolves around the sun. He was forced to recant and spent the rest of his life under house arrest.
aprofundar: The phrase eppur si moves, and yet it moves, is probably a legend: it does not appear in records of the time. On October 31, 1992, Pope John Paul II publicly acknowledged the error of the Galilean judges.
camada3: To reflect: it took three hundred and fifty-nine years for the institution to admit its mistake. How long does it take you to admit yours?

resposta: Between about 1400 and 1775, Europe prosecuted about a hundred thousand people for witchcraft and executed forty to sixty thousand, about eighty percent women. The handbook Malleus Maleficarum, the Hammer of the Witches, from 1486, helped spread the panic.
aprofundar: Important fact: Most executions were carried out by local and secular courts, and there were witch hunts in both Catholic and Protestant regions. The Spanish and Roman Inquisitions, interestingly, were more skeptical and executed fewer witches. Germany concentrated most of the deaths.
camada3: To contemplate: Fear of an invisible evil has turned neighbors into accusers. What panics today work the same way?

resposta: At the beginning of the sixteenth century, indulgences, the remission of the penalties of purgatory, were sold en masse. Part of the money paid for St. Peter's Basilica and Archbishop Albert of Mainz's debts to the Fugger bankers.
aprofundar: In 1517, Luther protested with his 95 theses. The Council of Trent banned the sale of indulgences in 1562. Say indulgences and Luther for the full story.
camada3: To contemplate: forgiveness sold is fear turned into money. Where does this exchange still take place today?

tema: The Doctrine of Discovery and Slavery
palavras: the doctrine of discovery and slavery
resposta: On June 18, 1452, Pope Nicholas V's bull Dum Diversas authorized the king of Portugal to subject Saracens and pagans to perpetual servitude. On May 4, 1493, the bull Inter caetera, by Alexander VI, gave Spain the newly discovered lands. These bills were used to justify colonization and slavery.
aprofundar: On March 30, 2023, the Vatican declared that the so-called doctrine of discovery is not part of Catholic teaching and that the bulls were used by colonial powers. The other side: religious men like Bartolomé de las Casas and, in Brazil, Father Antônio Vieira, denounced abuses against the natives, even though Vieira accepted African slavery.
camada3: To contemplate: a religious document turned entire peoples into property. What documents today define who is valuable and who is not?

resposta: From 1870 to 1997, about one hundred and fifty thousand indigenous children were taken from their families and put into boarding schools in Canada, most run by the Catholic Church and also by Protestant churches. More than 4,000 deaths have been documented, with estimates as high as 6,000.
aprofundar: In 2015, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission called the system cultural genocide: language ban, physical and sexual abuse, disease and starvation. In July 2022, in Maskwacis, Pope Francis apologized for the cooperation of many Catholics with this system.
camada3: To contemplate: these children were torn away to be saved. How many acts of violence have been committed in the name of saving someone?

resposta: In Ireland, from 1922 to 1996, Magdalene laundries, run by Catholic religious orders, confined women considered deviant, single mothers, orphans or poor to unpaid work. The most quoted estimate is about 30,000 women over the history of these institutions.
aprofundar: On 5 February 2013, the McAleese Report found significant involvement of the Irish State, and Prime Minister Enda Kenny issued an official apology. Religious orders have been criticized for not contributing to the repair fund.
camada3: To contemplate: the shame imposed on women has been transformed into free labor. Who profits when someone is declared unclean?

tema: Mother and baby homes in Ireland
palavras: mother and baby homes in ireland
resposta: The final report of the Irish Commission on Mother and Baby Homes, published on 12 January 2021, concluded that around nine thousand children died in eighteen institutions between 1922 and 1998, one in every seven born there. About fifty-six thousand women and fifty-seven thousand children passed through.
aprofundar: Many were run by Catholic orders. The case of Tuam, where remains of children were found in a sewer structure, shocked the country. The government issued a formal apology in 2021.
camada3: To contemplate: Children died because their mothers were considered sinners. Where else do you punish a child for judging a parent?

resposta: In May 2009, the Ryan Report of the Irish Commission to Investigate Child Abuse concluded that physical and emotional abuse was endemic in Catholic-run industrial and reformatory schools from 1936 onwards, and that sexual abuse was frequent in boys' institutions.
aprofundar: The report heard from over a thousand witnesses. It also showed that the State authorities failed to supervise. The names of many of the attackers have not been published because of a court case brought by the Christian Brothers.
camada3: To contemplate: the institutions protected their own name before the children. What do you protect first, your image or the truth?

tema: Sexual Abuse and Cover-up in the United States
palavras: sexual abuse and cover-up in the united states
resposta: In January 2002, the Boston Globe's Spotlight team revealed that the Archdiocese of Boston was transferring priests accused of abuse from parish to parish rather than removing them. Cardinal Bernard Law resigned later that year. The story was made into the film Spotlight, which won the Oscar for Best Picture in 2016.
aprofundar: In August 2018, a Pennsylvania grand jury reported more than three hundred accused priests in six dioceses and more than a thousand victims identified over the course of seventy years with systematic cover-ups. These figures refer to documented charges, not all of which went to trial, because many cases were already prescribed.
camada3: To contemplate: the crime was of individuals; the cover-up was of the institution. Pope Francis wrote in 2018 that saying no to abuse is saying no to all forms of clericalism.

resposta: In October 2021, the French independent commission CIASE, chaired by Jean-Marc Sauvé, estimated about two hundred and sixteen thousand victims of sexual abuse by clergy and religious in France since 1950, and about three hundred and thirty thousand including lay people who worked for the Church.
aprofundar: These are estimates made by statistical surveys with the population, not counting cases. The report spoke of the Church's deep and sometimes cruel indifference to victims for decades. The French bishops acknowledged institutional responsibility in November 2021.
camada3: To ponder: Why have so many victims remained silent for so long? Because sacred authority made their word impossible. Silence is also a structure.

tema: Ambrosian Bank and the Vatican Bank
palavras: ambrosian bank and the vatican bank
resposta: In 1982, Italy's Banco Ambrosiano collapsed with a hole of about 1.3 billion dollars. The Vatican Bank, the IOR, headed by Archbishop Paul Marcinkus, was its main shareholder. The president of the Ambrosiano, Roberto Calvi, was found hanged under Blackfriars Bridge in London in June 1982.
aprofundar: In 1984 the Vatican paid out about $244 million to creditors, acknowledging moral involvement, without admitting guilt. Calvi's death, first treated as suicide, was later ruled a homicide by Italian justice, but the defendants were acquitted in 2007.
camada3: To contemplate: money without transparency, protected by the sacred, becomes hiding place. Every institution that asks for donations must be held accountable.

palavras: stolen children in franco s spain
resposta: During Franco's dictatorship in Spain, children were taken from imprisoned, poor or unmarried mothers and given to other families, often with the participation of nuns, priests and doctors. Judge Baltasar Garzón estimated that some 30,000 children were in the custody of the regime between 1944 and 1954.
aprofundar: Larger numbers, such as three hundred thousand, are disputed and not supported by recent research. There were investigations and trials, but few convictions, partly by prescription; the first defendant brought to trial, a doctor, had the crimes proven but was acquitted by prescription in 2018.
camada3: To contemplate: mothers heard that the baby had died. A lie spoken with authority can last a lifetime. Who has the courage to seek the truth?

palavras: the church has asked for forfeiture
resposta: On March 12, 2000, Pope John Paul II celebrated the Day of Atonement, asking forgiveness for the sins of the children of the Church: intolerance and violence in the service of truth, divisions among Christians, the treatment of Jews, women and indigenous peoples.
aprofundar: He also apologized on other occasions: to Galileo in 1992; to the Orthodox for the sack of Constantinople in 2001. Pope Francis has apologized to Canada's indigenous people in 2022 and to the victims of abuse. The Church itself acknowledges that these events took place.
camada3: To contemplate: asking for forgiveness is the beginning, not the end. True forgiveness comes with repair and change. This applies to institutions and to each one of us.

palavras: about the jews and their lies
sobre os judeus e suas mentiras
resposta: In 1543, Martin Luther published On the Jews and Their Lies, in which he called for Jewish synagogues and schools to be burned, houses destroyed, and books confiscated. At the beginning of his career he had been more tolerant.
aprofundar: Centuries later, Nazi propagandists used that text. In 1994 the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America publicly repudiated these writings, and other Lutheran churches followed suit.
camada3: For contemplation: the same man who denounced the abuse of indulgences wrote a hateful text. No one is immune; not even reformers. That's why no leader should be above criticism.

resposta: On October 27, 1553, the physician and theologian Michael Servetus was burned alive in Champel, Geneva, for denying the Trinity. John Calvin helped prosecute him; he asked that he be beheaded rather than burned, but he supported the conviction.
aprofundar: Servetus was also wanted by the Catholic Inquisition: he was persecuted on both sides. In 1903, Protestants in Geneva erected an expiatory monument at the site, acknowledging the mistake.
camada3: To reflect: the Reformation was born claiming freedom of conscience and yet burned a dissident. Power tends to repeat what it fought. How can we avoid that?

resposta: In 1692 and 1693, in the Puritan colony of Massachusetts, more than two hundred people were accused of witchcraft in Salem. Nineteen were hanged, Giles Corey was crushed to death under stones for refusing to testify, and at least five died in prison.
aprofundar: The charges came from girls with seizures attributed to witchcraft, and the court accepted spectral evidence, visions and dreams. In 1697, the colony went on a fast for the mistake, and one of the judges, Samuel Sewall, publicly apologized. In 1711, there were reparations.
camada3: To contemplate: when someone's dream counts as evidence against you, there's no defense possible. Be suspicious of any system that accepts indictment without evidence.

tema: The Southern Baptist Convention and Slavery
palavras: the southern baptist convention and slavery
resposta: The Southern Baptist Convention, the largest Protestant denomination in the United States, was founded in 1845 after Northern Baptists refused to appoint slave-owning missionaries. It was therefore born in defense of the slaves.
aprofundar: In 1995, the Convention itself passed a resolution apologizing for slavery and support for racism. The other side: many Christians, like the Quakers since 1688, were voices for abolition, and black churches were the heart of the civil rights movement.
camada3: For contemplation: Bible texts have been used to defend and combat slavery. The difference wasn't in the book, it was in the heart and interest of the reader.

tema: Abuses at the Southern Baptist Convention
palavras: abuses at the southern baptist convention
resposta: In February 2019, the Houston Chronicle and San Antonio Express-News newspapers revealed about three hundred and eighty leaders and volunteers of Southern Baptist churches accused of sexual abuse since 1998, with more than seven hundred victims.
aprofundar: On May 22, 2022, Guidepost Solutions' independent report showed that for nearly two decades, members of the Convention's Executive Committee ignored and discouraged victims from avoiding prosecution, and that one official kept a secret list of hundreds of defendants.
camada3: To reflect: abuse is not a denominational problem; the pattern is the same as in the Catholic case: protecting the institution before the victims. Listen and believe the whistleblower, and go to the authorities.

resposta: On November 18, 1978, in Guyana, nine hundred and eighteen people died in connection with Pastor Jim Jones' People's Temple, most of them poisoned with cyanide, including more than three hundred children. Earlier, a U.S. congressman, Leo Ryan, and four other people were shot dead on the runway.
aprofundar: The People's Temple was affiliated with the Disciples of Christ, a Protestant denomination. Jones used many techniques of the BITE model: total isolation, confessions, death trials, fear of external enemies and a leader who could not be questioned.
camada3: To contemplate: many came here seeking justice and equality. The good intention of the follower does not protect the leader without limits. Say manipulation cues to recognize the cues.

resposta: In 1989, American television evangelist Jim Bakker was convicted of twenty-four counts of fraud for selling more vague lifetime memberships in his religious park than there were, and for using the money for personal luxury. He received a sentence of forty-five years, reduced to eight, and was paroled in 1994.
aprofundar: In 2020, Bakker was sued in the state of Missouri for selling a colloidal silver product as a Covid cure; the case ended in a settlement, with refunds to buyers.
camada3: To contemplate: the promise of eternity has been sold as real estate. Always ask yourself, where does the money go, and who's in charge?

resposta: In 1986 researcher James Randi demonstrated that televangelist Peter Popoff received by e-mail from his own wife the names and diseases he said were revealed by God. In 1988, preacher Jimmy Swaggart, who had condemned other pastors, tearfully confessed to a sex scandal and was excommunicated by his denomination.
aprofundar: Popoff continues to sell miracle products on television. The pattern in these cases: spectacle, promise of a miracle, request for money and no accountability.
camada3: To contemplate: those who most condemn the sin of others are not always those who live what they preach. Jesus said: "By their fruits you will recognize them".

resposta: In Brazil, pastor and former federal deputy Flordelis dos Santos de Souza was sentenced by a jury on November 13, 2022, to fifty years and twenty-eight days in prison as the mastermind of the murder of her husband, pastor Anderson do Carmo, who was shot dead in 2019 in Niterói. Sons and others involved were also convicted.
aprofundar: She had her mandate overturned by the House in August 2021. The case shows how a public religious image can hide violence inside the home. It's a crime of people, not of the evangelical faith.
camada3: To contemplate: the perfect family in the pulpit hid the opposite. Image is not proof of holiness. Find out more at the source link.

resposta: A portrait of Brazil today, with only verified facts. According to the IBGE 2022 Census, released in 2025, 56.7 percent of Brazilians declare themselves Catholics, 26.9 percent evangelicals and 9.3 percent without religion. The vast majority of communities are serious and welcoming. The problem arises where the usual formula comes together: power, more authority that cannot be questioned, more fear.
aprofundar: In this part of Pandora's Box are: tithing and campaigning, anointed objects and promised cures, mental illness treated as demonic, pressure on women, pulpit politics, misinformation, faith in television, debt forgiveness, and condemned crimes. Rule: accused is not convicted; here each case says exactly where you stand. Say themes from Pandora's box to see the list.
camada3: How to protect yourself: Ask any group three questions. Can I disagree without being punished? Where does the money go, and is there accountability? Do I walk out of here freer or more afraid?

palavras: donate the house to the church
doar a casa para a igreja
resposta: Today, the request for bids also arrives via PIX, QR code on screen and live broadcasts. Some campaigns call for high values or goods with a promise of blessing, such as the Holy Fire of the Universal Church. In March 2022, according to the Legal Counsel, the Court ordered Universal to return two hundred and four thousand reais donated by an ex-client; in other cases, the donors lost.
aprofundar: The mechanism is tithing as exchange: give what you don't have for God to act. A donation made under emotional pressure at the height of a cult can be challenged in court when there's coercion, but it's not always recoverable. Giving out of gratitude is free; giving out of fear or promise of return is business.
camada3: How to protect yourself: Never give away essentials, your home, your car, your family's savings. Decide at home, never at the service. Ask for accountability. And remember 2 Corinthians nine: not out of sadness or out of obligation.

tema: Articles of ointment and dressings for sale
palavras: articles of ointment and dressings for sale
resposta: Water, oil, salt, scarves, and seeds are offered as bearers of blessing or healing. In August 2020, the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office filed a public civil action against Pastor Valdemiro Santiago and the Worldwide Church of the Power of God for offering bean seeds, from a hundred to a thousand reais, with the promise of a cure for Covid; in October, a federal judge ordered the Ministry of Health to report that the bean has no proven efficacy.
aprofundar: Accuracy: In April 2022, according to the UOL, the São Paulo Public Prosecutor's Office requested the closure of the criminal investigation, stating that one of the videos that gave rise to the complaint had fraudulent editing. In other words: there was action and decision on health information, but no criminal conviction. This shows the double caution: to distrust the promise of a paid miracle, and also to check the accusation before it spreads.
camada3: How to protect yourself: No object replaces a treatment. Pray, if it's your faith, and follow the doctor. If someone tells you to stop taking your medicine, seek another medical opinion immediately.

resposta: Depression is a disease recognized by the World Health Organization, with treatment. Saying that it's just a demon, a sin, or a lack of faith can delay seeking help and increase the guilt of those already suffering.
aprofundar: What Brazilian research shows is balanced: studies reviewed in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry indicate that religiosity can protect mental health with support, meaning, and community. The damage happens when faith is used against treatment. Many pastors and priests today refer the faithful to a psychologist and psychiatrist, and that is the wise course.
camada3: How to protect yourself: faith and treatment can go hand in hand. If you are in distress, contact the health centre, CAPS or a psychologist; the CVV answers free of charge on 188, at any time.

resposta: Brazilian surveys of evangelical women who experienced domestic violence, published in psychology journals in 2021 and 2025, show that certain readings about submission, obedience, and preserving marriage at all costs helped maintain violent relationships and delay reporting.
aprofundar: The same studies show the paradox: faith has also been a source of strength for many to break out of the cycle. A survey of a shelter in São Paulo concluded that the problem is not religion itself but the patriarchal way in which it is taught in some churches, functioning as a means of controlling women.
camada3: How to Protect Yourself: No verse forces anyone to catch. The Maria da Penha Act of 2006 protects you. Call 180, the Women's Service Center, or 190 in an emergency.

resposta: The election law, Law 9,504 of 1997, Article 37, prohibits election propaganda inside temples of any religion. In August 2020, the Higher Electoral Court decided not to create its own category of abuse of religious power, but recalled that propaganda in temples and church donations are already prohibited. In 2022, the newspaper O Globo reported campaigns in churches that led worshippers to react and even change churches.
aprofundar: The other side: State reports in 2022 showed that many evangelical women listen to the pastor, but decide the vote by their own reflection. Faith and citizenship can go hand-in-hand; abuse is turning spiritual authority into electoral corral.
camada3: How to protect yourself: The vote is secret and yours. No leader can know who you voted for, and God has no party. If there's propaganda inside the temple, it can be reported by the Pardal app from Election Justice.

resposta: In the 2022 elections, UFRJ's NetLab lab, with Casa Galilea, monitored seventy-five evangelical YouTube channels, as well as pages and profiles, and found narratives of spiritual warfare and election fraud among the most engaging. BBC Brazil showed that fake news about an alleged persecution of evangelicals reached millions.
aprofundar: The mechanism is that of attention economy: the algorithm delivers more than it captures, and fear and outrage capture a lot. Thus, apocalyptic and common enemy content spreads more than messages of peace.
camada3: How to protect yourself: Check two serious vehicles before you stream; be wary of videos that call for urgency or say the media is hiding. Follow those who think differently, too, to puncture the bubble.

resposta: In 2015, according to Ancine, religious programs accounted for 21.1 percent of monitored public TV programming. On RedeTV, they were 43 percent of the grid, much of it in hours sold, or leased, to churches. Today, the struggle also happens in networks, with influential pastors and prosperity coaching.
aprofundar: Fact: TV concessions are public, and the sale of time to third parties is a long-standing topic of debate and lawsuits. Reading: Faith has also become an audience market, and audience is measured in donations.
camada3: How to protect yourself: Look at the time spent asking for money and selling products versus teaching. Real teaching doesn't need telemarketing.

tema: Immunity and Forgiveness of Churches' Debts
palavras: immunity and forgiveness of churches debts
resposta: The temples have immunity from taxes by the Constitution, Article 150, but it does not reach the contributions, like the CSLL and the social security. On March 17, 2021, Congress overrode a veto and excluded churches from the CSLL, nullifying past authorizations; the House voted 439 to 19 and the Senate, 73 to 1. The government has estimated renunciation of about 1.4 billion reais in four years.
aprofundar: According to the State, the Revenue had identified temples' maneuvers to distribute profits and remunerate pastors according to the number of faithful without paying these tributes; and the proposal was made by a deputy son of a church founder with debts to the Union. That was legal, voted and public; the question is ethical.
camada3: How to protect yourself: find out how your representatives vote. Immunity exists to protect freedom of worship, not profit.

resposta: In January 2007, the founders of the Renascer em Cristo church, Estevam and Sônia Hernandes, were arrested at Miami airport with about 56,000 dollars in undeclared cash, part of it hidden inside a Bible. They pleaded guilty and in August 2007 were sentenced in the United States to one hundred and forty days in prison, house arrest, and a fine.
aprofundar: This is a conviction case, so get in here. Other cases of religious leaders being investigated for embezzlement or money laundering in Brazil were left out when there was no verifiable official conviction or denunciation.
camada3: How to protect yourself: Churches are associations and can and should be accountable to their members. Ask for the financial statement. Whoever has nothing to hide shows it.

resposta: The medium João Teixeira de Faria, the John of God, who attended thousands of people in a nursing home in Abadiânia, Goiás, was denounced for sexual crimes against sixty-six victims. As of September 2023, according to the Goiás Court of Justice, he has been convicted in the first instance of fifty-six of them, with sentences totaling four hundred and eighty-nine years and four months. There are pending resources.
aprofundar: Victims reported that the abuse happened during supposed spiritual treatments, using the authority of a healer. He does not represent spiritism, nor the serious mediums, who, as Kardec taught, do not charge. The case began to fall apart in 2018, when women had the courage to speak on television.
camada3: How to protect yourself: No spiritual treatment requires isolation, undressing, or intimate contact. If it happens, go out and report it: dial 100 or 180.

resposta: There are recent cases with convictions. In November 2024, according to G1, a pastor from Guaraí, Tocantins, was sentenced to more than thirteen years in prison for raping and abusing ten teenagers; he used an alleged anointing ritual. In April 2024, another pastor from Tocantins was sentenced to nine years for raping a teenage girl inside the church.
aprofundar: The pattern is the same as seen in the world: spiritual authority creates trust and silence, and the institution sometimes protects the leader. For the sake of truth, here only come cases of conviction reported by a reliable source; this does not mean that they are the only ones, nor that every leadership is suspect.
camada3: How to protect yourself: Children should never be alone with leaders behind closed doors. Teach them that their bodies are theirs. Report it to Disk 100, which is anonymous.

resposta: Children take words literally. Repeatedly hearing about hell, demons, and the end of the world can generate lasting fear. Psychologist Marlene Winell called religious trauma syndrome the combination of anxiety, nightmares, and guilt that some adults report after a fundamentalist upbringing. It's not an official diagnosis, it's a description.
aprofundar: Teaching family values and faith is a parent's right. The difference is in the method: love and meaning form; terror and threat wound. Many people carry this fear with them even after they change their beliefs, and it can be treated.
camada3: How to protect yourself: If you were raised with fear, seek a psychologist, preferably one who respects your faith or lack of it. If you are a parent, talk about God as love and let your child ask questions. 1 John 4:18: perfect love throws out fear.

resposta: Some churches use, consciously or unconsciously, techniques that the psychology of persuasion describes: repetitive music, light, fatigue, collective catharsis, ever-successful testimonies, and multi-week chains, in which one small commitment leads to another larger one.
aprofundar: Robert Cialdini called this commitment and consistency: after saying a small yes, we tend to stay consistent with it. Add in the social proof, everybody's giving, and the scarcity, the opportunity is just today. The same techniques appear in sales and politics. Emotion is not a lie, but it's not proof.
camada3: How to protect yourself: Understand the script. When there's a request in the heat of the moment, wait until the next day. Ask: What testimonies of those who have not been cured have I never heard?
